{"command": "python3 -c '
import re

file_path = "/testbed/include/signal.h"

with open(file_path, "r") as f:
    content = f.read()

# Remove old definitions
content = re.sub(r"#define NULL_SIGNAL_SET \(\(sigset_t\)0x00000000\)\n", "", content)
content = re.sub(r"#define ALL_SIGNAL_SET  \(\(sigset_t\)0xffffffff\)\n", "", content)
content = re.sub(r"#define SIGNO2SET\(s\)    \(\(sigset_t\)1 << \(s\)\)\n", "", content)
content = re.sub(r"typedef uint32_t sigset_t;   /\* Bit set of 32 signals \*/\n", "", content)
content = re.sub(r"typedef uint32_t sigset_t;\n", "", content)

# Insert new definitions
new_defs = """
#if !defined(__KERNEL__) && !defined(__SIGSET_T_DEFINED)
typedef struct
{
  uint32_t s[_SIGSET_NWORDS];
} sigset_t;
#  define __SIGSET_T_DEFINED
#endif

#define __SIGSET_NWORDS _SIGSET_NWORDS

#define SIGSET_FMT "{ 0x%08" PRIx32 ", 0x%08" PRIx32 " }"
#define SIGSET_ELEM(p) (p)->s[0], (p)->s[1]

#define SIGSET_ZERO(p) \\
  do \\
    { \\
      (p)->s[0] = 0; \\
      (p)->s[1] = 0; \\
    } \\
  while (0)

#define SIGSET_FILL(p) \\
  do \\
    { \\
      (p)->s[0] = 0xffffffff; \\
      (p)->s[1] = 0xffffffff; \\
    } \\
  while (0)

#define SIGSET_ADD(p, s) ((p)->s[((s) - 1) >> 5] |= 1 << (((s) - 1) & 31))

#define SIGSET_DEL(p, s) ((p)->s[((s) - 1) >> 5] &= ~(1 << (((s) - 1) & 31)))

#define SIGSET_ISMEMBER(p, s) (((p)->s[((s) - 1) >> 5] & (1 << (((s) - 1) & 31))) != 0)

#define SIGSET_CLR(d) SIGSET_ZERO(d)

#define SIGSET_AND(d, s1, s2) \\
  do \\
    { \\
      (d)->s[0] = (s1)->s[0] & (s2)->s[0]; \\
      (d)->s[1] = (s1)->s[1] & (s2)->s[1]; \\
    } \\
  while (0)

#define SIGSET_OR(d, s1, s2) \\
  do \\
    { \\
      (d)->s[0] = (s1)->s[0] | (s2)->s[0]; \\
      (d)->s[1] = (s1)->s[1] | (s2)->s[1]; \\
    } \\
  while (0)

#define SIGSET_XOR(d, s1, s2) \\
  do \\
    { \\
      (d)->s[0] = (s1)->s[0] ^ (s2)->s[0]; \\
      (d)->s[1] = (s1)->s[1] ^ (s2)->s[1]; \\
    } \\
  while (0)

#define SIGSET_NAND(d, s1, s2) \\
  do \\
    { \\
      (d)->s[0] = ~((s1)->s[0] & (s2)->s[0]); \\
      (d)->s[1] = ~((s1)->s[1] & (s2)->s[1]); \\
    } \\
  while (0)

#define SIGSET_ISNULL(p) ((p)->s[0] == 0 && (p)->s[1] == 0)

#define SIGSET_COPY(d, s) \\
  do \\
    { \\
      (d)->s[0] = (s)->s[0]; \\
      (d)->s[1] = (s)->s[1]; \\
    } \\
  while (0)

#define SIGSET_EQUAL(s1, s2) \\
  ((s1)->s[0] == (s2)->s[0] && (s1)->s[1] == (s2)->s[1])

#define sigset_isequal(s1, s2) SIGSET_EQUAL(s1, s2)
#define sigset_isnull(p) SIGSET_ISNULL(p)
"""

# Find the location to insert the new definitions
# A good place is after the include guards and before other includes.
match = re.search(r"(#define __INCLUDE_SIGNAL_H\n)", content)
if match:
    insert_point = match.end()
    content = content[:insert_point] + new_defs + content[insert_point:]
else:
    # Fallback if the pattern is not found
    content = new_defs + content

with open(file_path, "w") as f:
    f.write(content)
'"}

More importantly, `nuttx/sched.h` only includes `nuttx/signal.h` (where the kernel `sigset_t` is defined) if `__KERNEL__` is *not* set, which is incorrect for kernel builds. I'll remove that `!defined(__KERNEL__)` condition in `nuttx/sched.h` and add the missing `limits.h` include to `signal.h`.

messages.content: The build failed again with `sigset_t` unknown type errors. The issue is in `nuttx/sched.h`: it uses `sigset_t` in `struct tcb_s` *before* including `nuttx/signal.h` where the kernel `sigset_t` is defined. I'll fix this by moving the `nuttx/signal.h` include to be immediately after the `signal.h` include, ensuring the type is defined before use. Rebuilding now.

function.arguments:
{"command": "python3 -c '
import re
file_path = "/testbed/include/nuttx/sched.h"
with open(file_path, "r") as f:
    content = f.read()

# Remove the old include location
content = content.replace("#ifdef CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL\n# include <nuttx/signal.h>\n#endif\n", "")

# Add it in the new location
new_include = "#include <signal.h>\n#ifdef CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL\n#  include <nuttx/signal.h>\n#endif\n"
content = re.sub(r"(#include <signal.h>\n)", r"\\1" + new_include, content, 1)


# The above regex replacement is tricky due to newlines. A simpler string replacement is better.
with open(file_path, "r") as f:
    content = f.read()
content = content.replace("#ifdef CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL\n# include <nuttx/signal.h>\n#endif\n", "")
content = content.replace("#include <signal.h>", "#include <signal.h>\n#ifdef CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL\n#  include <nuttx/signal.h>\n#endif")


with open(file_path, "w") as f:
    f.write(content)
'"}

    # Ensure there is no early include of nuttx/signal.h

    with open(file_path, "w") as f:

# Part 2: Remove sigset_t definition from nuttx/signal.h
file_path = "/testbed/include/nuttx/signal.h"
try:
    with open(file_path, "r") as f:
        content = f.read()
    content = re.sub(r"#ifdef __KERNEL__\n#if !defined\(__SIGSET_T_DEFINED\)\ntypedef struct\s*\{[^}]*\}\s*sigset_t;\n#\s*define __SIGSET_T_DEFINED\n#endif\n#endif\n", "", content, flags=re.S)
    with open(file_path, "w") as f:
        f.write(content)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error processing {file_path}: {e}")

    with open(file_path, "r") as f:

    # remove old definitions

    # add new generic one

#if !defined(__SIGSET_T_DEFINED)

{

} sigset_t;

#endif
"""
    if new_def not in content:
        content = re.sub(r"(#define __SIGSET_NWORDS _SIGSET_NWORDS\n)", r"\\1" + new_def, content, 1)

    with open(file_path, "w") as f:
        f.write(content)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error processing {file_path}: {e}")
'"}
